Given: A registered tab subscribes to the unregistered event name newFeature:changed on the user's channel.
When: Events arrive on another user's channel, under another event name, and then under the requested name on the correct channel.
Then: Only the matching event is forwarded, and a chat-event read still returns its existing row.
originalRegistration: Forward new user events without registering their names and keep chat reads available
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/startup-data-readiness.test.tsx — A private chat keeps its stored message while only its own detail event refreshes the recovery notice
userRiskAndJudgment: The wrong member and wrong topic both leave the recovery notice and original private message intact. Only the matching production topic refreshes it. No App consumer subscribes to the invented event name.
preAuditFinding: Searched Router subscribers and the worker topic registry for newFeature:changed. The worker has accepted arbitrary registered topic strings since #34736. The only matching application-tree call emits a negative control in startup-data-readiness.test.tsx. The registered production consumer never asks for this literal. The two-window, correctly addressed automation control in this batch delivered a first event to each original subscriber.
preAuditNextEntry: Need a supported caller subscribing to newFeature:changed. Wrong user, wrong name, correct delivery and retention of the existing chat row must be tested together.

Given: Two registered tabs subscribe to the same user-channel topic.
When: The topic emits an event, the connection suspends and reconnects, then the first tab disconnects and another event arrives.
Then: Both tabs receive the first event; a plain resume causes no resync, while reconnect causes one resync per tab. After the first tab disconnects, only the second receives the next event, and the shared subscription ends after the second disconnects.
originalRegistration: share one Worker realtime subscription until tabs disconnect
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-014 Each original subscriber receives its own resync and the last release ends the shared topic
userRiskAndJudgment: The independent provider sees the last actual topic release after A leaves and B receives its own subsequent delivery. Both subscriptions remain separately identified.
preAuditFinding: Two real tabs opened the same thread’s automation panel. Each subscribed once to the same user topic with its own ID. The first changed schedule reached both. Resuming a preserved channel yielded zero resyncs. A suspended connection followed by a continuity gap yielded one resync on each original ID. After A switched account, the next notification reached B alone. After B switched, the independent provider recorded unsubscribe for this exact topic on the original client. The separate presentation-shelf arm has multiple callbacks and was excluded from these counts.
preAuditNextEntry: Covered by independent provider receipts, both original subscription IDs, both visible schedules and final topic-specific release.

Given: Two registered tabs share an indicator read; the first tab's token is delayed and the second tab can provide a token immediately.
When: The second tab requests the indicators while the first token request is still pending.
Then: The read completes without waiting for the first tab and uses the second tab's bearer token. Both tabs receive token requests.
originalRegistration: Authenticate a shared read with the first successful tab without waiting for its sibling
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-020 The second window issues its read and supplies the successful credential while the first waits
userRiskAndJudgment: B owns a fresh indicator read, its successful credential and matching unread result while A is still waiting. Closing A first would change the failure mode.
preAuditFinding: Both tabs first registered on one native worker. Chromium temporarily froze the already-registered B window. One real indicators publication requested A’s credential, which remained held. Resuming B let it issue its own indicators read and respond immediately. The API receiver identified B, and the matching result on B contained the side thread’s unread timestamp before A supplied any credential. Both windows received token requests. Provider attribution uses aliases only.
preAuditNextEntry: Covered by the B-owned request, its exact result and the credential receiver while A was pending.

Given: Two registered tabs share an indicator read, and one token provider rejects while the other is pending.
When: The second token provider also rejects.
Then: The shared read rejects with AggregateError after every tab's token provider fails.
originalRegistration: Reject a shared read with AggregateError when every tab's token provider fails
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-023 The same pending indicators read returns the named aggregate to both callers
userRiskAndJudgment: The two credential rejections feed the same indicator computation. The original requests reject only after the second failure. Only the error name survives serialization; the successful sibling control still refreshes the indicator.
preAuditFinding: Two signed-in Windows registered on the same physical SharedWorker. A single chatIndicatorsChanged publication reached both. On each original port the active get-computed for chat-thread-indicators had no reply while A had failed and B was still held. Releasing B delivered a second credential failure, followed by error on each original request ID. The upstream worker uses Promise.any. The error on the wire contained only message and name. Both Windows saw a deserialized Error named AggregateError, with no AggregateError prototype or errors list. On the next control publication A still failed and B supplied the credential for a successful unread refresh. The frozen assertion matches reason.name. Snapshot errors were excluded.
preAuditNextEntry: Covered at the frozen named-rejection boundary. Preserving AggregateError instances or member reasons would require changing the serialization contract.

Given: Two tabs are registered.
When: The first tab disconnects and the second performs a cache-only read.
Then: The first tab's port closes, while the second tab's read succeeds with an empty result and its port remains open.
originalRegistration: Disconnect one tab without interrupting another tab
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-027 A released account port closes and the surviving registered window receives its empty offline query
userRiskAndJudgment: After A switches identities the worker-side observer sees its port close. B's cache-only read returns an empty array on B's own request, and B stays connected.
preAuditFinding: A and B registered against one worker. A selected a different signed-in account and the Clerk boundary held that selection. An independent worker observer saw disconnect followed by close on the first port. With the service offline B opened a different thread. Its own chat-event cache-only request returned an empty array with the same request ID and its port remained usable. Merely closing a browser tab had not produced the worker-side close receipt in the control.
preAuditNextEntry: Covered by real account release, independent worker-side port close and B’s cache-only result.

Given: A tab has not registered with the bridge.
When: It attempts a cache-only chat-event query.
Then: The query rejects because tab registration is required.
originalRegistration: Reject shared-data access before the tab is registered
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/workspace-transcript-isolation.test.ts — worker-runtime-002 Reopening a conversation reads only rows belonging to the member's selected workspace
userRiskAndJudgment: The frozen actor bypasses registration before its first cache read. The actual client registers first and guards requests with requireRegistration. Cross-account transcript disclosure is a different Given. The selected-workspace transcript test asserts isolation across organizations only; see the separate member-switch and project-cache controls.

Given: A registered tab has unread indicators and chat-message notification subscriptions, with one chat row initially available.
When: Indicator-change and read-cursor events arrive, then two chat-message notifications arrive two seconds apart as another row becomes available.
Then: The indicator and read-cursor events cause three indicator reloads and no catch-up requests. Each chat-message notification triggers one catch-up, and the cached rows advance from one row to two.
originalRegistration: Warm unread chats only after chat message notifications
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-033 The registered tab reloads indicators three times before two messages advance its offline history
userRiskAndJudgment: A reader receives indicator and cursor changes without a transcript catch-up, then separately catches up each message event. Both rows render when reopened offline.
preAuditFinding: A registered Chat tab started with one cached message. The independent window port received two indicator reloads for chatIndicatorsChanged and one for chatThreadReadCursorUpdated. Neither publication generated catch-up. Two real chat-message publications two seconds apart each generated one catch-up, returning zero then one new row from cursor 1. Reopening the original thread offline rendered both original and new messages. The registered page test independently verifies the unread badge, cursor update and transcript.
preAuditNextEntry: Covered by the Router history test and exact native invalidation, catch-up and offline controls.

Given: A user has two subscribers to the same user-scoped topic, another subscriber to that topic in the organization scope, and a subscriber to a different user-scoped topic on one port.
When: The first user subscriber is released, then the remaining user subscriber is released and later reacquired.
Then: After the first release, notifications reach the second user subscriber, organization subscriber, and different-topic subscriber, but not the released subscriber. Releasing the second removes only that user-topic subscription; the organization and different-topic subscriptions remain. A reacquired subscriber receives a later notification.
originalRegistration: Keep scopes, topics, and subscriber releases independent on one port
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/startup-data-readiness.test.tsx — A private chat keeps its stored message while only its own detail event refreshes the recovery notice || turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/member-template-library.test.ts — chat-composer-custom-templates-026 Sharing a private board updates the catalog audience
userRiskAndJudgment: Wrong member or organization traffic does not update the wrong audience. Two-window delivery, followed by a surviving recipient after release, is also covered by the batch 112 native topic test. Four manually arranged callbacks on a single port add no distinct consumer.
preAuditFinding: Inspected both real producers of presentationTemplatesChanged. On a single registered port the two libraries allocated separate user subscriber IDs, separate organization IDs and subscriptions to other topics. Both libraries bind to the same authenticated root lifetime. Leaving the shelf does not cancel either root subscriber. The new account-switch control releases the whole registered connection and the other topics along with it.
preAuditNextEntry: Need separate production release controls for the two user subscribers on the same port, with the organization and other topic remaining live through release and reacquisition.

Given: A subscriber begins attaching to a realtime topic, but the attach is delayed.
When: The subscriber is cancelled and a new subscriber with the same ID starts attaching before the old attach completes; then both attaches complete.
Then: The cancelled subscription rejects with an AbortError. Only the new subscriber receives a subsequent notification, and the worker sends one successful subscription reply for the reused ID without an error reply.
originalRegistration: Ignore a stale subscription attach after cancellation and reacquisition
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-038 Both waiting ports receive the attach failure and the reacquired subscription delivers to its new owner
userRiskAndJudgment: The worker allocates fresh subscriber IDs for normal reacquisition. The old recipient gets no new item, and the new owner actually receives an event. Deliberate reuse of a discarded ID requires an internal caller.
preAuditFinding: Held a real provider attach, closed its waiting Window, opened a second Window before release and then published to the surviving subscriber. The independent observer received different generated IDs. Checked realtime.ts, which allocates crypto.randomUUID per subscription, and the old-subscriber release path. Neither page navigation nor a transport resume selects a previously used ID. No original AbortError receipt was observed.
preAuditNextEntry: Need a supported caller that can cancel and reuse its original ID before the attach finishes, with the original rejection and exactly one successful subscription reply observable.

Given: Two ports subscribe to the same realtime topic while its shared attach is pending.
When: The attach fails, then one port reacquires the subscription.
Then: Both subscriptions reject with the attach failure, and the failed topic is no longer subscribed. After reacquisition, a notification reaches the new subscriber.
originalRegistration: Deliver an attach failure to every subscriber and permit reacquisition
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-038 Both waiting ports receive the attach failure and the reacquired subscription delivers to its new owner
userRiskAndJudgment: Both subscribers receive the failed attachment on their original IDs. The same B document returns from Side survey to Primary survey, reacquires with a new ID and renders the newly published Maple schedule. The replay uses a held HTTP attach response that returned 503 and a new delivery on B after the failed topic has zero receivers.
preAuditFinding: While the user channel was attaching, A and B opened the same thread and issued a subscription for its exact automation topic. A terminal attach failure returned realtime-subscription-error on both original IDs. Publishing to that topic reached zero registered provider callbacks. B navigated to the side thread and back in the same Window on the same port, obtained a fresh subscribed ID and received the next publication. Its panel changed from Cedar to Maple.
preAuditNextEntry: Covered by both original error receipts, provider delivery-0 and the new B subscriber’s normal notification.

Given: Two separate worker Stores each have a subscriber with the same ID and topic.
When: The first worker Store is reset and a notification is sent to the topic.
Then: The first worker's signal is aborted and its port closes with no remaining listeners, while the second worker remains active and its subscriber receives the notification. The second worker can still complete a cached chat-data query with an empty result.
originalRegistration: Keep identical subscription keys in separate worker Stores independent
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/workspace-transcript-isolation.test.ts — worker-runtime-002 Reopening a conversation reads only rows belonging to the member's selected workspace || test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-027 A released account port closes and the surviving registered window receives its empty offline query
userRiskAndJudgment: The surviving domain can receive its own update and read its local history after the other instance stops. A matching hand-assigned subscriber key across unrelated Stores and a precise listener count belong to the fixture.
preAuditFinding: Read the production SharedWorker entry, which gives the worker AbortSignal.any([]) for its global lifetime. Account switching exercised closure of a particular peer and a successful empty read on the survivor. The new separate-context presentation probe timed out before both shelves were ready. Prior isolated-worker delivery remains a control. Neither action demonstrates a resettable worker signal or a reused subscriber ID in two domains.
preAuditNextEntry: Need a supported worker reset observable outside the destroyed domain, the same subscriber ID in both domains, proof that the first lost its listeners and the survivor’s own cache-only result.

Given: An authenticated user has one chat event cached locally, and the initial server catch-up request is held pending.
When: The user opens the conversation, allows catch-up to return a second event, then a realtime notification exposes a third event.
Then: The cached event appears before catch-up completes; afterward the conversation contains events in sequence 1, 2, 3. Catch-up requests use successively increasing cursors without duplicates, and no new request starts after the conversation's lifecycle is reset.
originalRegistration: Show cached chat data before catching up live
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/returning-transcript-cursors.test.ts — A returning %s reader follows the expense cursors across two deliveries and leaves for a new chat [direct and message-port]
userRiskAndJudgment: Both direct and message-port rows show the cached expense first and then exactly three ordered entries. After leaving, the new chat remains usable. Additional harmless fetches after exit are not part of this user risk.

Given: A production app has a configured telemetry token and an authenticated shared-worker bridge.
When: The client queries cached chat events after sequence 42 for a private thread.
Then: The query succeeds with an empty result and produces one production client-telemetry event identifying a successful cache-only chat-event query. The event includes duration but omits the private thread ID, sequence cursor, and entity-specific resource data.
originalRegistration: Reports production shared worker queries without entity identifiers
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/cached-chat-telemetry.test.ts — Production telemetry control reports the empty private conversation before its first remote message || turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/cached-chat-telemetry.test.ts — single-connection-client-002 a preview conversation finishes its empty local read without publishing query telemetry
userRiskAndJudgment: The production control reads the empty private conversation with safe operation metadata, and preview suppresses production telemetry. A cache-only read has no input sequence cursor to expose.

Given: The thread snapshot endpoint returns a presigned object URL whose contents include a stored conversation.
When: The runtime catches up on thread metadata and then reads it from cache only.
Then: Both reads return the stored conversation as the snapshot with no events.
originalRegistration: Load a chat thread snapshot from its presigned object URL
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/workspace-snapshot-inspection.test.ts — A reopened workspace shows its downloaded conversation before a later rename is delivered
userRiskAndJudgment: The signed download makes the conversation readable across reopen before the delayed rename. The previous 403 and offline controls distinguish the download from a later catch-up. The raw snapshot/events pair is internal.

Given: A batched catch-up request covers two threads, one with no new events and one with a new event.
When: The runtime performs the batched chat catch-up.
Then: It reports only the thread with new events, and cache-only reads show an empty list for the unchanged thread and the new row for the updated thread.
originalRegistration: Report only non-empty tails from a batched chat catch-up
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/returning-transcript-cursors.test.ts — Only the updated conversation gains a message when the worker warms two open threads
userRiskAndJudgment: A batch warms the changed conversation and leaves its neighbor empty. Reopening offline checks stored messages at their own destination; membership in an intermediate array adds no outcome.

Given: A matching one-use bootstrap response and a different network response are available for a feature-switch request.
When: The client makes three successive requests, with the third carrying an abort signal.
Then: The first request returns the bootstrap response without obtaining a token or using the network; the next two return the network response, and the token provider is called once per network request with the corresponding signal.
originalRegistration: uses a matching bootstrap response once before falling back to the network
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/lab-page/__tests__/lab-feature-catalog.test.ts — Lab reads the embedded Banking preference before showing the service's later updates
userRiskAndJudgment: The actual Lab control displays the embedded preference, then reflects authenticated service updates. Counting SDK calls and comparing AbortSignal object identity would freeze the adapter.

Given: The Clerk user value is null, and the session then enters a transition.
When: A reader waits for the user while transitioning, then the session signs in as user-a and the transition ends.
Then: The read stays pending during the transition and resolves to user-a rather than reporting sign-out.
originalRegistration: The transitive state defers the value instead of reporting a sign-out
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/workspace-invitations.test.tsx — clerk-user-003 An invitation waiting through sign-in belongs to the first settled member
userRiskAndJudgment: The original invitation waits and completes with A's membership after the current account becomes B. B cannot produce the same invitation result.
preAuditFinding: The signed-in invitation page was held at feature startup, set to signed out and then transitioned before releasing bootstrap. The invitation remained pending. Clerk published user-a and then user-b in the same turn. Only A’s member resource belonged to the invited Field team. The original invitation completion displayed Invitation accepted for Field team after B became current. invitation-redirect.ts reads the membership from the awaited original user.
preAuditNextEntry: Covered by the pending UI and distinct member resources. The original consumer identifies A even after the current identity becomes B.

Given: Clerk is signed in as user-a, and an owner is initializing user state.
When: A reader requests the user value synchronously before owner initialization finishes.
Then: The read is a promise the owner can resolve and eventually resolves to user-a.
originalRegistration: An owner claims the signal before it resolves the Clerk runtime
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/auth-v1/__tests__/identity-startup.test.ts — The workspace starts its member subscription after a delayed identity load
userRiskAndJudgment: The member control and its scoped subscription both wait for Clerk and identify the right member once loaded. Reading the same deferred during the synchronous bootstrap prologue has no independent page action.
preAuditFinding: Traced the synchronous bootstrap prologue through setupClerkUser$, shared database initialization and authenticated realtime. The owner claims the deferred before awaiting Clerk. The bridge awaits Clerk/session identity, and authenticated realtime starts only after locale and feature switches. Even the HTML bootstrap response is consumed after featureSwitches$ has awaited clerk$, so an embedded response cannot advance this consumer past the held SDK. The reachable downstream subscriber can identify the resolved member, but it does not return the exact read requested synchronously before owner initialization finished.
preAuditNextEntry: Need a public reader whose invocation can be observed before the owner completes and whose own pending result resolves to A. A later user-scoped notification alone cannot discriminate that timing.

Given: Clerk user state has settled for user-a under an active owner.
When: The owner is replaced, then Clerk emits while the session is transitioning.
Then: The last published user value remains available as the same settled promise resolving to user-a; the new event is not observed.
originalRegistration: Aborting the owner keeps the last published value and stops listening
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/auth-v1/__tests__/identity-startup.test.ts — Only the replacement workspace receives the member profile after the owner changes
userRiskAndJudgment: The disposed menu stays absent while the successor receives the new member profile. The existing same-member and identity-change handoff controls distinguish update from replacement. Retrieving the disposed owner's settled promise is internal.
preAuditFinding: Extended the same-member handoff control from 005. Held the original onboarding handoff after its service request, disposed its owner, installed a new Workflows owner for the same member and session, then emitted a Clerk transition. Released the held original and awaited its original Router readiness. It rejected with AbortError and the original prompt was absent. The successor’s member control was visible. The exposed promise belongs to the disposed operation and does not expose the old settled user promise.
preAuditNextEntry: Need an already-issued public observation preserving the old settled promise itself and its A value through replacement and the transition. The aborted onboarding operation cannot witness that identity.

Given: A signed-in user has realtime subscriptions routed through the SharedWorker.
When: The app subscribes to a user-scoped connector-permission update and the worker receives a matching event.
Then: The subscription is registered with the worker, the app handles the event once and completes the wait, and no app-side Ably authentication token is requested. The subscription is removed after completion.
originalRegistration: Route app subscriptions through the SharedWorker without an App Ably client
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/permission-allow/__tests__/permission-allow-page.test.tsx — The permission review changes with consecutive Slack grant notifications
userRiskAndJudgment: Two consecutive notifications on the same mounted permission review change its decision controls. Production uses the worker; the one-shot wait and exact provider-auth count describe subscriber implementation.
preAuditFinding: Enumerated the production waitAbly*Until callers. Link waits for wallet:changed and connector setup waits for connector:changed. The permission review and host authorization consumers subscribe to connectorPermissionUpdated, but their subscriptions persist across notifications. A successful last-topic release was independently observed for Chat automations in 014. It cannot establish completion of the original permission waiter.
preAuditNextEntry: Need a supported one-shot user-scoped connector-permission subscriber. Observe its first matching event, completion, worker-only authentication and release at the independent provider.

Given: A signed-in user requests a live update, but the realtime-token service responds with HTTP 500.
When: Realtime setup and the pending subscription attempt to connect.
Then: Both reject with an Ably connection failure, no live subscription remains, and a later subscription request also rejects with an Ably connection failure.
originalRegistration: Realtime authentication failure does not leave stale live updates
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/111/README.md#realtime-005
userRiskAndJudgment: The real auth failure and later read leave the conversation usable, while the failed-topic and reacquisition controls protect stale subscription delivery. A new recovery promise after terminal failure was not a success requirement in the frozen row.

Given: Realtime is suspended and a subscriber is waiting for a channel attachment.
When: The user cancels that subscriber while attachment is pending.
Then: The wait rejects with the subscriber’s cancellation reason, and its channel subscription is removed.
originalRegistration: Cancelling a subscriber releases its pending channel attach wait
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-014 Each original subscriber receives its own resync and the last release ends the shared topic || test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-038 Both waiting ports receive the attach failure and the reacquired subscription delivers to its new owner
userRiskAndJudgment: A leaves a pending subscription, B stays active, then the provider records the final release. Observing a canceled listener's reason by reference adds no separate result.

Given: A signed-in user starts a background subscription while the transport is suspended and provides an error callback.
When: The channel later reports a terminal “connection failed” error.
Then: The callback receives that error, and the channel subscription is removed.
originalRegistration: A background subscription reports a terminal channel failure after returning
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/111/README.md#realtime-010 || test-rebuild-evidence/112/registered-ports.native.test.mjs — message-port-014 Each original subscriber receives its own resync and the last release ends the shared topic
userRiskAndJudgment: Terminal channel failure disposes the subscriber. Discontinuous reconnection of a healthy consumer refreshes its schedule. A background error callback's original object has no page consumer.

Given: A signed-in user creates a payload subscription with `runOnSubscribe` omitted.
When: The subscription receives a payload, then the transport disconnects and reconnects.
Then: Initialization runs once on subscription and once after reconnection; the payload is handled, and the continuity gap triggers recovery.
originalRegistration: Payload initialization with runOnSubscribe=undefined retains events and gap recovery
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/okou-page/__tests__/settings-wallet.test.tsx — realtime-011 Link settings refresh on subscription, handle the member event, and recover missed changes
userRiskAndJudgment: The original mounted subscriber receives the payload and distinct gap refresh. An ordinary reconnection control does not introduce an extra refresh.
preAuditFinding: Link settings uses the production wallet:changed payload subscriber with runOnSubscribe omitted. Held its external user-channel subscription until the initial Connect page had rendered. Attaching refreshed to Update permissions. A member payload refreshed it to Connected. After suspension a missed server change appeared as Reconnect required when the transport reconnected. The separate service-receiver diagnostic observed one status read in each of these three bounded phases.
preAuditNextEntry: Covered by the registered Link settings journey and independently counted receiver phases.

Given: A signed-in user subscribes to chat-thread live updates, but the initial subscription refresh fails.
When: Subscription initialization throws an error.
Then: The subscription request rejects with the initialization error, but the chat-thread automations live subscription remains active.
originalRegistration: An initial refresh failure does not destroy live subscriptions
representative: test-rebuild-evidence/111/README.md#realtime-020
userRiskAndJudgment: A failed initial detail read leaves the mounted panel subscribed. An independent later automation publication changes Cedar to Maple while the withheld control does not. The caller's initialization exception is internal.

Given: The browser fails to construct the shared database worker.
When: Bridge setup is attempted and a consumer checks its connection.
Then: Both operations reject with the original worker-construction error.
originalRegistration: Expose worker construction failures to bridge consumers
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/__tests__/workspace-worker-startup.test.ts — shared-worker-preload-002 An early failure on the matching preload reaches the interruption dialog || turbo/apps/platform/src/views/__tests__/workspace-worker-startup.test.ts — shared-worker-failure-002 Two native worker failures interrupt the open page and flush a single report
userRiskAndJudgment: Construction throws before a connection exists. The frozen assertion compares the error received by setup and a second connection reader. The interruption tests exercise a real user-facing worker failure. A new retry UI for synchronous constructor failure is outside the frozen Then.

Given: A CDP connection is open, but its Browser.getVersion probe receives no response before the 31-second deadline.
When: The probe deadline expires and the client makes a Target.getTargets request.
Then: The version probe rejects as a read-only protocol failure, while Target.getTargets still succeeds with an empty target list.
originalRegistration: a version-probe deadline leaves the CDP connection usable
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/browser-session/__tests__/browser-response-deadlines.test.tsx — A new-tab action reads the inventory after the outstanding version probe expires
userRiskAndJudgment: An optional version lookup can expire and the same connection subsequently inventories targets and admits a working tab. A read-only exception class adds no user protection.

Given: A viewer has two pending CDP requests on an open connection to a remote browser.
When: The viewer closes and then attempts to notify the browser.
Then: Both pending requests reject, and no notification is sent after closing; the remote browser is not closed by this action.
originalRegistration: closing a viewer rejects pending requests without closing the remote browser
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/browser-session/__tests__/browser-response-deadlines.test.tsx — Leaving the viewer retires two outstanding requests without closing its remote page
userRiskAndJudgment: The dismissed viewer loses input and releases its connection while its remote page survives the outstanding replies. The exported browser's lifetime is independently observed.

Given: A native browser attachment is pending on a CDP connection, with its request associated with the original parent session.
When: The operation is cancelled, a later Browser.getVersion request is made, and the attachment response arrives late.
Then: The attachment request rejects with AbortError, the connection remains usable, and the late attachment is detached using the original parent session.
originalRegistration: raw native attachment cancellation preserves its original parent session
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/signals/browser/__tests__/client.test.ts — Moving a page during attachment releases its late session and leaves the original page interactive
userRiskAndJudgment: Retain original parent ownership of a late child detach on a surviving connection. The existing page-move case cleans up a child but has no original native parent; the extension-client peer deletes the child by ID alone. A particular version call and the exact cancellation text are unnecessary.
retainedGap: Observe the late detach on its original, still-surviving parent, with a working sibling or connection.
adjacentObservation: Cancellation text, version sampling counts and hypothetical cross-member leaks are outside this judgment.
preAuditFinding: Traced native attachment and its late-response callback through the real viewer. native.ts captures the parent session for Target.detachFromTarget. The earlier tab-move arm produced a detach without the original parent, while leaving the actual viewer closes its connection. The version latency sampler can run on a separate frames connection, which cannot establish that the cancelled parent connection was usable.
preAuditNextEntry: Need an independently cancellable native child with its originating parent kept alive, an observable AbortError, a successful version call on that exact connection and the late detach addressed to the same parent.

Given: Native bridge startup has sent a browser-target attachment request on an open CDP connection.
When: Startup is cancelled and the attachment response arrives late.
Then: Startup rejects with AbortError, the late native attachment is detached, and the connection remains usable for Browser.getVersion.
originalRegistration: cancelling native bridge startup releases its late original attachment
representative: turbo/apps/platform/src/views/browser-session/__tests__/browser-viewer-binding.test.tsx — browser-viewer-binding-$id changes transport before the initial binding is ready
userRiskAndJudgment: Changing binding during startup leaves the new endpoint selected and usable. The package late-attach test releases the returned top-level session and its listener. Sampling a version on the discarded connection adds no user effect.
preAuditFinding: Followed the real native bridge startup owner, its pending browser-target attach and cancellation path.
